points:
A live example, not slides.
The idea system in this repository, walked end to end.
The point: skill vs. command vs. subagent vs. tool.
And why one decision stays behind a command only the owner types.

/orient — what this agent can do here, right now.
Every command, skill and tool is read from disk at run time.
Not from a stored list.
An empty category is reported as empty, not guessed.

/idea — recording an idea through the sanctioned writer.
Hands the idea to tools/append_idea.py.
It assigns an id and validates the entry.
The idea log is append-only: no line is ever edited or deleted.

/idea-triage — a subagent reads the idea and reports.
Finds related plans and documents.
Writes one finding.
Can move the idea to triaged, and no further — deliberately.

Plan beat — from idea to governed work.
The idea becomes a requirement, a plan, backlog phases.
The same hand-off every piece of work here goes through.
No command runs during this step.

Overview-skill rebuild — one script, run, reported.
The d-system-overview skill calls tools/generate_overview.py.
It reports exactly what the script printed.
It never recomputes a number itself.

Test — the same page, updated with real data.
The overview now shows the idea just recorded.
Not a placeholder.
Terminal and talking points keep working through the same run.

Four different things, one protected boundary.
A skill, a command, a subagent and a tool each do a different job.
/session-close stays behind a command a person types.
No agent can reach it.
